issues.t: 5.3L V8 burns oil
issues.sym: You need to add oil between changes, sometimes a quart every 1,000-2,000 miles. You may see blue smoke at startup, fouled spark plugs, misfires, or a low-oil warning.
issues.why: On the Active Fuel Management 5.3L, oil gets past the piston rings and is also pulled in through the cylinder deactivation system, so the engine burns it. This is the most-reported problem on 2007 Avalanches.
issues.next: Check the oil level every fill-up and never let it run low, because that can ruin the engine. A shop can measure consumption and suggest fixes, from a valve cover baffle update to new piston rings.

issues.t: Collapsed cylinder deactivation lifter
issues.sym: A steady ticking or tapping from the engine, a rough idle, misfires, and a flashing check engine light.
issues.why: The special lifters that let the engine shut off half its cylinders to save fuel can stick or collapse. Once one fails, the camshaft lobe under it can also wear.
issues.next: Don't ignore a new tick with a misfire code. Have the lifters checked soon; replacing the lifters (and the camshaft if it's worn) is a big job, and waiting can make it bigger.

issues.t: 4-speed automatic slips or fails
issues.sym: Harsh or late shifts, the engine revs without the truck speeding up, no reverse, or no 3rd and 4th gear. It often fails completely around 50,000-100,000 miles.
issues.why: The 4L60-E automatic behind the 5.3L has weak internal parts that wear out, especially when towing or hauling. Heat makes it worse.
issues.next: Check the fluid for a burnt smell or dark color and get it looked at quickly. Most failed units need a rebuild or a remanufactured transmission. An auxiliary cooler helps if you tow.

issues.t: Cracked dashboard
issues.sym: Cracks open up in the top of the dashboard, often near the passenger airbag cover or the defrost vents.
issues.why: The dash material on this generation shrinks and cracks with sun and heat over time.
issues.next: A dash cover or cap hides the cracks cheaply. Make sure nothing blocks or weighs down the passenger airbag cover; a full dash replacement is a big labor job.

issues.t: Instrument cluster gauges stick or quit
issues.sym: The speedometer, fuel, temperature or other gauges stick, read wrong, or drop to zero, and the dash display may flicker.
issues.why: The small stepper motors that drive the gauge needles in GM's 2003-2006 full-size truck clusters fail. GM offered special coverage for a time.
issues.next: Have the cluster tested. A repair shop can replace the stepper motors or rebuild the cluster, which is usually cheaper than a new one.

issues.t: "Service 4WD" message and 4WD won't engage
issues.sym: A Service 4WD message or light comes on, the 4WD buttons blink, and the truck won't shift into or out of four-wheel drive. The check engine light may also come on.
issues.why: The transfer case shift motor's position sensor (encoder) or the 4WD selector switch fails, so the 4WD module can't tell what gear the transfer case is in.
issues.next: Have the 4WD codes read. The fix is often a new encoder motor or selector switch; until then, avoid needing 4WD in bad weather.

issues.t: Heater and A/C blend door actuator clicking or stuck
issues.sym: A clicking or tapping noise behind the dash, air coming out the wrong vents, or the temperature stuck on hot or cold on one or both sides.
issues.why: The small electric motors (actuators) that move the doors inside the heater box strip their plastic gears or fail.
issues.next: Note which control doesn't respond and have the actuator replaced. Some are easy to reach behind the dash, others take longer.

issues.t: Fuel gauge reads wrong
issues.sym: The fuel gauge reads empty when the tank is full, jumps around, or stays stuck, and the low-fuel light may come on at the wrong time.
issues.why: The fuel level sensor on the in-tank fuel pump module wears out.
issues.next: Track mileage between fill-ups so you don't run out. The sensor is part of the fuel pump module, so many owners replace the whole module.

issues.t: Fuel pump failure
issues.sym: Long cranking before it starts, stalling, sputtering under load, or cranking without starting at all.
issues.why: The in-tank electric fuel pump on GM's 2000-2006 full-size trucks and SUVs wears out with age and mileage.
issues.next: Have fuel pressure tested before replacing parts. The fix is a new fuel pump module, which also fixes a bad fuel gauge sensor at the same time.

issues.t: Corroded battery cable ends
issues.sym: Slow cranking, a click with no start, dim lights, or white or green crust on the battery terminals.
issues.why: The battery cable ends on these trucks corrode easily, which blocks current to the starter.
issues.next: Clean the terminals and check the cable ends. If the corrosion has gone up into the cable, replace the cable end or the cable.

issues.t: Tailgate handle breaks or tailgate won't latch
issues.sym: The tailgate handle cracks or flops loosely, and the tailgate won't open or won't latch shut.
issues.why: The plastic tailgate handle and its parts weaken with sun and age, and then break.
issues.next: Replace the handle with a good-quality part. Check the latch rods inside the tailgate at the same time.

issues.t: Clunk felt in the steering wheel
issues.sym: A clunk or knock you feel in the steering wheel when turning slowly, such as in parking lots.
issues.why: The intermediate steering shaft between the steering column and gear binds as it slides. GM issued a service bulletin for these trucks to lubricate or replace the shaft.
issues.next: This is not usually dangerous. A shop can grease or replace the intermediate shaft to stop the noise.

issues.t: Rusted brake lines can burst
issues.sym: The brake pedal suddenly goes soft or to the floor, and brake fluid may be dripping near a wheel or under the frame.
issues.why: The steel brake lines on GM's early-2000s full-size trucks rust, especially in salt states, and can burst. Federal regulators investigated this but no recall was issued.
issues.next: Have the brake lines inspected at every oil change if you live where roads are salted. Replace rusted lines before they fail.

issues.t: Tailgate support cables can snap (recall)
issues.sym: The tailgate drops past level when opened, or a support cable looks rusty or frayed.
issues.why: The tailgate support cables can corrode and break, letting the tailgate fall. GM recall 04V-129 replaces the cables.
issues.next: Don't sit on or load the open tailgate until the cables are checked. Check your VIN for open recall 04V-129.

issues.t: ABS kicks in at low speed (recall)
issues.sym: The brake pedal pulses and the ABS buzzes when you're stopping slowly on dry pavement, and the truck takes longer to stop.
issues.why: Corrosion at the wheel speed sensors can make the ABS think a wheel is locking when it isn't. GM recall 05V-379 addresses it.
issues.next: Leave more stopping distance until it's fixed. Check your VIN for open recall 05V-379.

issues.t: Hydro-Boost brake booster can leak (recall)
issues.sym: Power steering fluid leaking near the brake booster, and the brake pedal or steering suddenly feels harder to push or turn.
issues.why: On some trucks the Hydro-Boost brake booster, which uses power steering pressure, has a relief valve bore or pressure accumulator that can crack and leak. GM recalls 04V-045 and 05V-043 inspect and replace it.
issues.next: If braking or steering suddenly takes more effort, pull over and have it towed. Check your VIN for open recalls 04V-045 and 05V-043.

issues.t: Frame crossmember can puncture the fuel tank in a crash (recall)
issues.sym: No symptom in normal driving. In a severe front crash on the left side, the tank could be punctured and leak fuel.
issues.why: A mid-frame crossmember can tear in certain crashes and puncture the fuel tank, creating a fire risk. GM recall 03V-019 adds protection.
issues.next: Check your VIN for open recall 03V-019 and have it done for free.

issues.t: Fuel rail damper clip can break and leak fuel (recall)
issues.sym: A strong gasoline smell from the engine bay, or wet fuel on top of the engine.
issues.why: The clip holding the fuel pulse damper on the fuel rail can crack, letting the damper loosen and fuel leak onto a hot engine. GM recall 06V-289 fixes it.
issues.next: If you smell fuel, don't drive it. Check your VIN for open recall 06V-289.

issues.t: Rear middle seat belt can ride up on the stomach (recall)
issues.sym: The lap part of the second-row center seat belt is hard to keep low across the hips, especially for smaller passengers.
issues.why: The way the center belt was routed lets the lap belt ride up onto the abdomen, which raises the risk of injury in a crash. GM recall 05V-163 changes the belt.
issues.next: Check your VIN for open recall 05V-163. Until it's fixed, seat children in boosters or car seats in the outboard positions.

issues.t: Gear position display may stay dark (recall)
issues.sym: The gear indicator in the instrument cluster doesn't light up after starting, so you can't see which gear you're in.
issues.why: Under certain starting conditions the shift position display in the cluster may not light. GM recall 05V-055 reprograms the cluster.
issues.next: Look at the shifter itself to confirm the gear. Check your VIN for open recall 05V-055.

issues.t: Wrong load capacity on the tire label (recall)
issues.sym: No symptom. The tire and loading label on the door jamb lists the wrong cargo and passenger capacity.
issues.why: Some trucks shipped with a label showing an inaccurate vehicle capacity weight, which could lead to overloading. GM recall 05V-552 supplies a corrected label.
issues.next: Check your VIN for open recall 05V-552 and get the corrected label.

issues.t: Heated washer fluid module can overheat (recall)
issues.sym: A burning smell or smoke from under the hood, washers or other electrical items not working.
issues.why: The heated windshield washer module can short and overheat, which can start a fire. GM recall 08V-441 tried a fix and recall 10V-240 disabled the system.
issues.next: Check your VIN for open recalls 08V-441 and 10V-240 and have them done.

issues.t: Passenger airbag inflator can rupture (recall)
issues.sym: No warning beforehand. In a crash the passenger airbag could burst and spray metal pieces.
issues.why: The passenger airbag inflators (made by Takata) can break down after years of heat and humidity. GM recalls 21V-050 through 21V-054 replace them.
issues.next: Check your VIN at once for an open airbag recall and get it fixed for free. Until then, avoid using the front passenger seat if possible.

issues.t: Water can damage the fuel pump control module (recall)
issues.sym: The engine stalls, won't start, or has electrical faults, especially after rain or washing.
issues.why: A seal on the fuel system control module can separate and let water in. GM recall 09V-154 repairs it.
issues.next: Check your VIN for open recall 09V-154.

issues.t: Ignition key can stick in Start or snap back (recall)
issues.sym: The key stays in the Start position after the engine starts, or springs back to Accessory and shuts the engine off while driving.
issues.why: The ignition lock actuator can bind. If the key falls to Accessory while moving, you lose engine power, power steering and power brakes, and the airbags may not deploy. GM recall 14V-827 fixes it.
issues.next: Check your VIN for open recall 14V-827. If the engine shuts off, steer firmly and brake hard to stop safely.

issues.t: Faded and chalky body cladding
issues.sym: The gray plastic cladding on the doors, fenders and bed rails turns pale, chalky or blotchy.
issues.why: The unpainted plastic trim on the first-generation Avalanche breaks down in sunlight.
issues.next: A trim restorer or plastic dye brings the color back for a while. Painting the cladding is a longer-lasting fix.
